video_summary: This video provides an introductory overview of neuroscience, the multidisciplinary scientific study of how the brain and nervous system operate. It highlights fundamental questions regarding brain function and outlines several key subfields of neuroscience research: developmental, molecular, cellular, systems, behavioral, and cognitive neuroscience.

visuals.description: Title slide with a 3D digital rendering of neurons and synapses in the background.
Thought bubbles presenting fundamental questions about brain function, leading to the term 'NEUROSCIENCE'.
visuals.visible_text: HOW DOES MY BRAIN WORK? How am I able to see? How can I remember and forget things? How am I able to learn new things? How am I able to feel? NEUROSCIENCE

visuals.description: Slide listing the primary research goal of neuroscientists regarding disorders.
visuals.visible_text:
RESEARCH by NEUROSCIENTISTS
- Understand nervous system disorders

visuals.description: Branching tree diagram detailing the major subfields of neuroscience research.
visuals.visible_text:
RESEARCH by NEUROSCIENTISTS
- Understand nervous system disorders

NEUROSCIENCE
- Developmental Neuroscience: Development of the brain
- Molecular Neuroscience: Molecular level processes
- Cellular Neuroscience: Neurons, Glial cells and their function
- Systems Neuroscience: Neural Circuit functioning
- Behavioural Neuroscience: Neural mechanisms of behaviour
- Cognitive Neuroscience: Neural mechanisms of mental processes

visuals.description: Concluding slide highlighting the ongoing expansion of neuroscience research.
visuals.visible_text: There is more to research and more to learn!
